briefing.executive_summary:
The competitive landscape for project management tools in 2025 is characterized by a diverse array of offerings, each catering to different segments of the market. Linear, known for its speed and developer-centric design, faces competition from Height, Shortcut, Plane, and Agiled. Height positions itself as a direct competitor to Linear, emphasizing its AI capabilities and similar workflow efficiency. Shortcut, formerly Clubhouse, offers a more flexible approach with customizable workflows, appealing to teams that require adaptability. Plane distinguishes itself with an open-source model and self-hosting options, appealing to teams that prioritize data control and customization. Agiled, on the other hand, targets a broader audience with its all-in-one platform that integrates project management with other business functions like CRM and invoicing.

Each competitor has carved out a niche by focusing on specific features and customer needs. Height's strong AI integration and free tier make it attractive to teams looking for advanced automation without a high cost. Shortcut's emphasis on flexibility and integration with developer tools makes it a strong choice for engineering teams. Plane's open-source nature and cost-effective pricing appeal to teams that value customization and control. Agiled's comprehensive suite of business tools positions it as a solution for small to medium-sized businesses looking to consolidate their software stack. Overall, the market is competitive, with each player leveraging unique strengths to capture different segments of the project management space.

competitors.name: Height

pricing.content: Height offers a freemium pricing model with four main tiers: Free, Team, Business, and Enterprise. The Free plan includes unlimited tasks, views, and integrations for unlimited members. The Team plan costs $8.50 per user per month when billed monthly, or $6.99 when billed annually, and includes 100MB of storage. The Business plan is priced at $14.99 per user per month billed monthly, or $11.99 annually, offering 1GB of storage and priority support. The Enterprise plan requires a custom quote and includes advanced administrative and security features.

sources.summary: Height pricing ranges from Free to $15 per user/month as of July 2026, with 4 plans available including a free tier.
Height's Team plan is $8.50/month billed monthly or $6.99/month billed annually; Business plan is $14.99/month billed monthly or $11.99/month billed annually.
Height offers a Free plan, Team plan at $8.50/month billed monthly or $6.99/month billed annually, and Business plan at $14.99/month billed monthly or $11.99/month billed annually.

key_features.content: Height's key features include robust automation capabilities, allowing users to set up workflows and triggers to streamline project management. It supports between 100 and 2,500 automations per month depending on the plan. The platform offers various project visualization tools such as spreadsheets, Kanban boards, calendars, and Gantt charts. Height also includes real-time chat, time tracking, and AI-generated task lists to enhance productivity and collaboration.

sources.summary: Height features built-in automation, allowing 100-2,500 automations per month, and offers project visualization tools like charts and timelines.
Height includes project management essentials, real-time chat, time tracking, and project visualization tools like Kanban and Gantt charts.
Height offers visualizations for tasks in calendar, Kanban, or Gantt chart views, and supports organizing tasks with multiple teams.

market_positioning.content: Height positions itself as an AI-powered project management platform designed to help teams manage projects, automate tasks, and collaborate efficiently. It emphasizes its automation capabilities and real-time collaboration features. Height is marketed as a versatile tool suitable for various industries, offering integrations and reporting analytics similar to its competitors. However, it lacks some of the deeper AI integrations and security features that competitors like Linear offer.

sources.summary: Height positions as an AI-powered project management platform with real-time collaboration and integrations, but lacks Linear's deeper AI integration and security features.

target_audience.content: Height targets teams and organizations looking for efficient project management solutions with a focus on automation and collaboration. It is suitable for fast-growing teams managing multiple cross-functional workstreams, as well as diverse teams across entire organizations. Height's features cater to industries such as entertainment, education, healthcare, IT, and e-learning, making it a versatile choice for businesses seeking to streamline their project management processes.

sources.summary: Heights Platform is used in industries like entertainment, education, healthcare, IT, and e-learning.

recent_developments.content: In recent years, Height has secured $14 million in Series A funding to enhance market awareness, product innovation, and hiring strategies. This funding round was led by Redpoint Ventures, highlighting the platform's potential to address ongoing challenges in project management. Height has also released public access to its platform, aiming to expand its user base and improve its offerings for enterprise clients.

sources.summary: Height secured $14 million in Series A funding to build market awareness and support product innovation and hiring.

key_threats: Height's freemium model with a robust free tier offers unlimited tasks and integrations, challenging competitors to match its value proposition without eroding margins.
The platform's strong automation capabilities, allowing up to 2,500 automations per month, can significantly enhance productivity, posing a threat to less automated competitors.
Height's competitive pricing, especially the Team plan at $6.99/user/month annually, undercuts many competitors, making it attractive for cost-sensitive teams.
opportunities: Height lacks comprehensive AI integration compared to competitors like Linear; enhancing AI features could attract more tech-savvy users.
The platform could improve its security and governance features to appeal to enterprise clients who prioritize data protection.
Height's current visualization tools could be expanded with more advanced analytics and reporting capabilities to better serve data-driven teams.

competitors.name: Shortcut

pricing.content: Shortcut offers three main pricing plans: Team, Business, and Enterprise. The Team plan is priced at $10 per user per month, with an annual prepayment discount reducing it to $8.50 per user per month. The Business plan costs $16 per user per month, or $12 with annual prepayment. The Enterprise plan offers custom pricing tailored to specific needs. A free version is available for teams of up to 10 users, and a free trial is also offered.

sources.summary: Shortcut has 3 pricing plans starting at $10 per user per month, with a free version and trial available.
The Team Plan is $10/user per month or $8.50 if paid annually; Business Plan is $16/user per month or $12 annually.
Pricing starts at $8.50 per user per year for the Team plan, with a free version available.

key_features.content: Shortcut is a project management platform designed for software teams, offering features like issue tracking, sprint planning, and roadmap coordination. It supports customizable workflows, milestone tracking, and multiple workspaces. The platform integrates with major developer tools like GitHub and GitLab, facilitating agile execution across cross-functional teams. Shortcut's flexibility allows for structured planning and management of multi-team programs.

sources.summary: Shortcut includes customizable workflows, milestone tracking, multiple workspaces, and third-party integration.
Shortcut integrates with major dev tools like GitHub and GitLab, supporting structured planning and agile execution.
Shortcut is designed for structured product planning with agile execution across cross-functional teams.

market_positioning.content: Shortcut positions itself as a flexible project management tool suitable for growing teams that require coordination across multiple squads. It offers more adaptability than Linear, with custom workflows and milestones, making it ideal for businesses needing cross-functional collaboration. While Linear is known for speed and simplicity, Shortcut balances ease of use with the needs of larger teams, making it particularly useful for tech companies in dynamic business environments.

sources.summary: Shortcut offers more flexibility with custom workflows and milestones, suitable for teams needing adaptable solutions.
Shortcut is tailored for businesses coordinating multiple squads, offering flexible workflows and strong collaboration features.
Shortcut is more structured and feature-rich, better suited for teams needing cross-team planning and agile constructs.

target_audience.content: Shortcut targets software development teams that require a balance between structured planning and agile execution. It is particularly beneficial for growing tech companies that need to manage multiple projects and coordinate cross-functional teams. The platform is designed to support product development, but it also accommodates marketing and other departments that need to work closely with product teams, making it versatile for various business needs.

sources.summary: Shortcut is used by marketing and product teams for collaboration, supporting cross-functional coordination.
Shortcut helps businesses streamline processes like lead nurturing and customer feedback, useful for tech companies.

recent_developments.content: In a recent development, Shortcut announced a $25 million Series B funding round led by Greylock Partners. This funding will be used to enhance the platform's flexibility and integration capabilities, ensuring it remains user-friendly and efficient. The investment also aims to expand Shortcut's market presence and improve its core functionalities, making it more appealing to a broader range of users.

sources.summary: Shortcut closed a $25M Series B funding round led by Greylock Partners to enhance platform flexibility and integration.

key_threats: Shortcut offers a free version for teams up to 10 users, which could attract small teams away from Linear's paid plans.
The customizable workflows and milestones in Shortcut provide flexibility that Linear's fixed status model cannot match.
Shortcut's integration with major developer tools like GitHub and GitLab enhances its appeal to tech teams, challenging Linear's developer focus.
opportunities: Shortcut's UI is less polished than Linear's; Linear should emphasize its superior design to attract users who value aesthetics.
Shortcut's reporting capabilities are not best-in-class; Linear could enhance its analytics features to appeal to data-driven teams.
Shortcut's market presence is smaller due to its rebranding; Linear can capitalize on its stronger brand recognition to capture market share.

competitors.name: Plane

pricing.content: Plane offers a transparent and straightforward pricing model with no hidden fees or minimum charges. For contractors, the cost is $39 per month per person, which includes payments in over 240 countries and 70+ local currencies. For hiring and paying international employees, the price is $499 per month per person, covering hiring in 100+ countries, locally compliant contracts, and additional benefits like health insurance. The HRIS platform is free, allowing management of all team members on a single platform without any monthly charges.

sources.summary: Plane charges $39/month per contractor and $499/month per international employee, with no setup fees or hidden costs.

key_features.content: Plane is a comprehensive project management solution with features designed for various teams, including Engineering, Marketing, and Operations. It offers multiple view options, cycle management, and real-time collaboration powered by Yjs. The platform supports rich text editing, activity tracking, and role-based access control, making it versatile for different organizational needs. Additionally, Plane provides API access and offline support with sync on reconnect, enhancing its usability and integration capabilities.

sources.summary: Plane offers comprehensive project management with features like cycle management, real-time collaboration, and multiple view options.

market_positioning.content: Plane positions itself as a versatile tool suitable for various teams beyond just engineering, unlike Linear which focuses on EPD teams. It emphasizes adaptability to team needs with features like multi-channel intake and workflows that cater to different departmental requirements. Plane's broader approach makes it a strong choice for organizations seeking an all-in-one system that supports diverse team functions, including customer-facing roles.

sources.summary: Plane is positioned as a versatile tool for multiple teams, offering features like multi-channel intake and adaptable workflows.

key_threats: Plane's pricing model is highly competitive with no hidden fees, making it attractive to cost-sensitive customers.
The ability to hire and pay international employees in 100+ countries without setting up local entities is a significant advantage.
Real-time collaboration and offline support features enhance user experience, potentially drawing users from less interactive platforms.
opportunities: Plane lacks specific features for social and collaborative playlist creation, which could be an area for Linear to exploit by enhancing its social features.
The absence of a dedicated focus on engineering and product development teams could allow Linear to strengthen its position in these niches.
Plane's broader team focus might dilute its effectiveness for specialized teams, providing an opportunity for Linear to offer more tailored solutions.

competitors.name: Agiled

pricing.content: Agiled offers a range of pricing plans tailored to different user needs. The Basic plan is free, while the Pro plan costs $7.99 per user per month, and the Premium plan is priced at $11.99 per user per month when billed annually. Monthly billing is available at $9.99 and $14.99 per user for Pro and Premium plans, respectively. Additional features such as extra automations, pipelines, and storage can be added for a small fee per user per month.

sources.summary: Agiled offers three plans: Basic (free), Pro ($7.99/user/month), and Premium ($11.99/user/month) with annual billing. Monthly billing costs $9.99 and $14.99 per user for Pro and Premium plans, respectively.
Agiled's pricing includes a free plan, Starter at $29/month, Pro at $69/month, and Scale at $129/month, with extra seats available as add-ons.
Agiled's pricing is per-user-tier, with core features available on all paid plans starting at $30/month. The top tier costs $249/month for 15 seats.

key_features.content: Agiled is a comprehensive platform offering features such as CRM with pipeline management, AI-powered proposals, contracts with e-signatures, invoicing, project management with Kanban and Gantt charts, time tracking, and scheduling. It includes a client portal where clients can view invoices and project status. Agiled also provides HR capabilities like employee management and attendance tracking, making it suitable for small to mid-size agencies.

sources.summary: Agiled includes CRM, AI-powered proposals, contracts with e-signatures, invoicing, project management, time tracking, and scheduling. It also offers HR features like employee management and attendance tracking.
Agiled features a client portal, native invoicing with Stripe and PayPal, contracts with e-signature, and CRM automation. It also offers booking page generation with payment-on-booking.

market_positioning.content: Agiled positions itself as an all-in-one solution for small businesses and agencies, emphasizing its comprehensive feature set that covers the entire business lifecycle. It targets solo freelancers and small agencies looking for a cost-effective, full-stack platform. Agiled differentiates itself by offering a wide range of integrated tools, including CRM, project management, and HR capabilities, which are typically spread across multiple platforms.

sources.summary: Agiled is positioned as an all-in-one platform for small businesses and agencies, offering CRM, accounting, projects, helpdesk, and marketing tools.

target_audience.content: Agiled primarily targets small businesses, solo freelancers, and small agencies. It is designed for those who need a comprehensive suite of tools to manage CRM, accounting, projects, and marketing without the complexity and cost of multiple separate systems. The platform is particularly appealing to businesses with up to 10 employees, where its breadth of features provides significant value.

sources.summary: Agiled is best for 10+ employee businesses ready to standardize on one vendor across CRM, accounting, projects, helpdesk, and marketing.

key_threats: Agiled's comprehensive feature set, including CRM, project management, and HR tools, offers a one-stop solution that can attract small businesses looking to consolidate their software stack.
The competitive pricing of Agiled, with a free plan and affordable paid tiers, makes it an attractive option for cost-conscious small businesses and freelancers.
Agiled's integration of AI features for proposals and reports provides advanced capabilities that can appeal to tech-savvy users looking for automation.
opportunities: Agiled lacks advanced reporting and analytics features, which Linear could enhance to attract data-driven businesses.
The absence of collaborative features like shared playlists or social integrations in Agiled's offering presents an opportunity for Linear to differentiate with enhanced team collaboration tools.
Agiled's pricing model, which charges per user, could be undercut by Linear offering more flexible or flat-rate pricing plans to attract larger teams.

recommended_actions.action: Enhance AI capabilities to match or exceed Height's offering.
recommended_actions.rationale: AI is a key differentiator in the market, and enhancing these capabilities could significantly improve competitive positioning.

recommended_actions.action: Develop a comprehensive business suite similar to Agiled.
recommended_actions.rationale: Offering a broader suite of tools could attract a wider range of customers, but it requires significant development effort.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce a self-hosting option to appeal to privacy-conscious customers.
recommended_actions.rationale: Self-hosting can attract customers who prioritize data control, aligning with Plane's unique offering.

recommended_actions.action: Expand integration capabilities with more developer tools.
recommended_actions.rationale: Improving integration with popular developer tools can enhance appeal to engineering teams, a core market segment.

recommended_actions.action: Consider an open-source model to increase adoption and community engagement.
recommended_actions.rationale: Open-source can drive community-driven improvements and increase adoption, but it requires a shift in business model.
